title: What Ecommerce Playbook Is and Why It Matters
summary: The foundations of ecommerce playbook: what it is and why getting it right pays off.
body:
Starting an online store in 2026: pick a niche, validate demand, choose a platform (Shopify, Etsy, WooCommerce), and launch lean. Most profitable stores start under $1,000.

title: Getting Started: Your First Five Moves in Ecommerce Playbook
summary: Start ecommerce playbook this week with five concrete moves.
body:
Don't try to do everything. Do these five, in order:

1. Pick a niche you understand
2. Validate: 10+ strangers would buy
3. Source or make 5-20 SKUs
4. Choose platform; build the store
5. Photograph everything well

Five moves, one week. Momentum beats perfection — the rest of this guide builds on exactly this start.

title: Common Ecommerce Playbook Mistakes and How to Avoid Them
summary: The mistakes everyone makes with ecommerce playbook — and the fixes.
body:
The classic errors:

- Building before validating demand → Fix: address it in your first week, not after it costs you.
- Pricing too low to survive → Fix: address it in your first week, not after it costs you.
- Ignoring email capture → Fix: address it in your first week, not after it costs you.
- Spending on ads before the store converts → Fix: address it in your first week, not after it costs you.

Every mistake above is cheap to prevent and expensive to repair. Prevention is the whole game.

title: Ecommerce Playbook Beginner FAQ
summary: Straight answers to the most common ecommerce playbook questions.
body:
Q: Dropship or hold inventory?
A: Hold a little inventory; dropshipping quality is hard to control.

Q: How much to start?
A: $500-$1,000 lean is realistic.

Q: LLC needed day one?
A: Sole proprietor is fine to start; form an LLC when revenue is steady.

Still stuck? Start with record 2 of this guide and do the first move today.

title: Ecommerce Playbook: Safety, Legal, and Fine Print
summary: What to watch out for with ecommerce playbook: safety, contracts, and fine print.
body:
Read before you act: Building before validating demand And: Pricing too low to survive

General rules: get agreements in writing, understand what you're signing, keep records of money in and out, and know when a professional (lawyer, accountant, vet, doctor — depending on the domain) is worth the fee. An hour of professional advice beats a month of fixing.
